subject: STABLE encode-cpu-opus (gate-green 13:24-13:45): async submission + early-scheduled path under 0108 semantics, pre-0108 sync fallback, TEGU_PERF_ASYNC proof line, chain executor hook; host CA-loop numbers
body:
GATES
- run_host_tests 13:45: all offline GPU tests passed. This includes the new bridge test for a pre-0108 kernel.
- CA: PASS. Render: 32 baseline. Async frontend: 6/6, ASan and release.
- Integration: only the known CA pass failure (checks=1005, required_failures=2).
- iOS -Werror syntax check with the full defines: rc=0.

FILES (md5)
- compute_frontend.m d111c8cb
- tests/nord2_metal_bridge_test.c 306eb0e4
- tools/frame_bench_main.m bbd795c8, tools/frame_bench.py 61029a3e
- nord2_metal_bridge.c d475ec50: comment only from me in async_probe; the rest is lowering-opus's work.

WHAT
1) Kernel semantics, per KA 0108:
- P11+ answers WAIT_SEQ(0) with {4}, so async turns on. P8-P10 (NotFound) stay synchronous with one WAIT per job, i.e. C6o behaviour. The bridge probe is unchanged.
- The test fake now models 0108. An opt-in seq0_notfound flag models pre-0108, and a new test asserts 3 draws give 3 WAITs and 0 WAIT_SEQ.
2) New device proof line, TEGU_PERF_ASYNC, one per perf window, next to TEGU_PERF_FRAME:
- bridge_async: 0 = sync fallback, 1 = WAIT_SEQ.
- async_cmds / sync_cmds.
- deferred: completion moved to the finish FIFO.
- early: CA's scheduled handlers ran at submission.
- nodefer_shadow: queued but held back by a shadow read-back.
- mid_reaps: reaps before CPU blits.
- sched_us: commit -> scheduled-handler latency, mean/max.
On P13 expect bridge_async=1, early ~= commands, and sched_us ~= submit CPU instead of the whole execute time.
3) Chain hook (lowering-opus API, off by default):
- begin/end around the job loop; reply 0 counts as in-chain.
- Completion seq = max(last id, chain id). A chain_end error fails the command.

HOST MEASUREMENT: frame_bench FB_CA_LOOP, 100 frames, scenario large, 46 jobs/frame
Device-calibrated fake time model. CA work = FB_CA_US, job prep = FB_SUBMIT_US, GPU = FB_GPU_US. These are wall-time sleeps, not spins: the host is in a quota slice beside other jobs.
- Sustained-heavy calibration (CA+encode 13 ms, submit CPU 11.4 ms, GPU+kernel 8.1 ms):
  - sync (C6o): 42.1 ms/frame, CA blocked 28.0 ms per commit
  - async: 30.4 ms, CA blocked 16.2
  - async + finish FIFO / early: 29.8 ms, CA blocked 15.7, early=68 of 74
  - => -12.3 ms
- Blur calibration (CA 25 ms, submit CPU 19.2, GPU+kernel 15):
  - sync 68.5 -> async + early 49.8 ms (-18.7)
- The host sync baseline is inflated by about 0.2 ms of sleep overshoot per per-job WAIT.

DEVICE-CALIBRATED ESTIMATE (lag-analysis section 2 numbers)
- CA's thread is now released when the last job is submitted: the submit CPU plus about 65 us of kernel queue/clean per job, not CPU+GPU+wait.
- Sustained heavy: execute on CA's path 19.5 -> ~12.3 ms. 33.6 -> ~26.3 ms (-7.3 ms, ~38 fps).
- Blur: 34.2 -> ~20.6 ms. 61 -> ~47 ms (-13.6, ~21 fps).
- The report's -17 to -20 needs the submit CPU itself off CA's path:
  (a) report scheduled at commit. This needs a kernel 'pending writer' reservation on the target surface at commit; otherwise 0097(c) cannot hold a swap whose jobs are not yet submitted. Kernel ABI, KA.
  (b) cut the submit CPU (chaining, per-draw cost).
  (c) CPU DVFS.
- With (a): frame ~= max(CA+encode ~14, submit ~12, GPU ~8) -> ~60 fps sustained.

RISK
- First device use of async. Kill switches: NORD2_METAL_ASYNC=0, NORD2_METAL_EARLY_SCHEDULED=0.
- Host-harness note: sync mode plus my host finish-FIFO thread crashes in frame_bench's pool drain. Cause is the host NSObject's non-atomic refcount; this is not production code.
